newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bremen cotton buyers shun high nearby prices.
newsitem.headline: Bremen cotton buyers shun high nearby prices.

text.p: European spinning mills are looking for nearby cover but refuse to pay higher sellers' prices, a report from the Bremen Cotton Exchange said on Monday.
Consumers were looking to replace unfulfilled Central Asian supply contracts but failed to secure adequate volumes and qualities, the fortnightly market report said.
Buyers also baulked at dollar-induced price rises which have added seven percent to mark prices since the start of the year.

The Exchange reported upland cotton trades in Central Asian standards 1-4, Chad and Israel-Acala, Mexico-Juarez and Indian high grades, Argentine medium grades and West African and Zimbabwean descriptions up to third quarter 1997.
In the longstaple sector, it reported trades in Egyptian Giza 86 and Giza 77, Central Asian and U.S.-Pima cotton, and Israel-Pima, all for spot through third quarter.
